value: behavioural response threshold of 90 dB re 1 µPa for megalopae to replayed reef sound (the lowest level tested)

source.authors: Jenni A. Stanley, Craig A. Radford, Andrew G. Jeffs
source.title: Behavioural Response Thresholds in New Zealand Crab Megalopae to Ambient Underwater Sound

method: behavioural bioassay: time to metamorphosis (TTM) of megalopae in loudspeaker-equipped water baths under replayed North Reef ambient sound at 135, 126, 100 and 90 dB re 1 µPa plus a Silent treatment; threshold = lowest level at which TTM was significantly shorter than in the Silent treatment; TTM compared by Kruskal-Wallis then Dunn's pairwise procedure
conditions: Wild megalopae caught in light traps within 500 m of shore near Leigh Marine Laboratory, north-eastern New Zealand, October to December 2010, held at ambient water temperature (15-22 C) under natural light. Each treatment had three replicate water baths with 5-10 vials of one megalopa each (about 15-30 per treatment); the Figure 2 caption gives n = 75 for L. variegatus. Levels were measured with a calibrated hydrophone in the tanks, not calculated; megalopae were randomly allocated to treatment and replicate only when more than 150 were caught in a night, and the paper describes no other ordering. 90 dB was the lowest level tested, so the true threshold may lie lower. The threshold is a metamorphosis-timing response to a settlement cue, not an audiogram or a neural hearing threshold. The same sentence gives C. lavauxi 100 dB and H. sexdentatus 126 dB; the Discussion gives 125 dB for H. sexdentatus, so those two are not filed. Reef sound from an unfavourable (sandy-beach) habitat produced no significant TTM change in the reef species.
quote: Leptograpsus variegatus had the lowest behavioural response threshold of 90 dB, followed by C. lavauxi with a threshold of 100 dB, and lastly H. sexdentatus with 126 dB re 1 µPa.
note: Whole Results sentence (31 words) read intact in two abutting pieces ('Leptograpsus variegatus had ... followed by C. lavauxi' | 'with a threshold of 100 dB, and lastly H. sexdentatus with 126 dB re 1 µPa.'); the preceding sentence ends '...consistently had the shortest median TTM.' and the following one begins 'The median TTM did not differ significantly', so the sentence is whole. Only the L. variegatus clause is used for the value. Family Grapsidae as printed in the paper; order left blank because the paper does not state it and OBIS (obis.org) was refused. Name Leptograpsus variegatus EXACT ACCEPTED in main's docs/views/gaps/gbif-names.tsv; C. lavauxi and H. sexdentatus are absent from that file, so they are not filed (owner question). Not on main: git grep of pone.0028572 and Leptograpsus over the whole docs/ tree finds only desk-d228/d230 progress notes listing it as an unread lead, and no d23x/d24x evidence or unit branch holds it. source.authors: Bo-Mi Kim, Seunghyun Kang, Do-Hwan Ahn, Jin-Hyoung Kim, Inhye Ahn, Chi-Woo Lee, Joo-Lae Cho, Gi-Sik Min, Hyun Park
source.title: First Insights into the Subterranean Crustacean Bathynellacea Transcriptome: Transcriptionally Reduced Opsin Repertoire and Evidence of Conserved Homeostasis Regulatory Mechanisms

method: de novo whole-body transcriptome (Illumina MiSeq 2x300 bp; 74,866 contigs assembled with Oases; N50 1,302 bp); about 111 known opsin, arthropsin, peropsin and melanopsin protein sequences searched against the contigs by local BLASTx
conditions: Wild, subterranean specimens from Hongcheon-Gun, Gangwon-Do, South Korea (collection date not stated); whole bodies of 15 adults pooled for one RNA extraction, so this is one pooled transcriptome, not a per-animal result. A zero is absence from the transcriptome, not proof the genome lacks opsin genes: the paper reports no BUSCO or core-gene completeness statistic and no E-value for the opsin search, and says many of the eye-related genes it checked were also not detected. The authors call the result a potential regressive adaptation to the dark environment; that interpretation is theirs.
quote: Interestingly, in the A. bangokensis transcriptome, we were not able to identify an opsin contig.
